youtube.title: Why Car Tires Are Always Black 🛞 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Natural rubber is pale, and early car tires were whitish and wore out quickly. Around 1912 tire makers began mixing carbon black, a fine soot made by burning oil or gas, into the rubber. Carbon black strengthens the rubber and blocks the ultraviolet light that cracks it, so tires last many times longer. The black colour is a side effect of that reinforcement.
